multiplicity_control.source_excerpt: 9.1.1 Statistical hypotheses; 9.1.2 Multiplicity adjustment: "tralokinumab over placebo will be tested using a 1-sided test at the 2.5% level against the null" "If the primary endpoint demonstrates that tralokinumab is superior to placebo in achieving a" "higher response rate of IGA-AHE score of 0 (clear) or 1 (almost clear) at Week 16, then a 5%" "level will be passed to the key secondary endpoints where superiority of tralokinumab over" "The primary and key secondary endpoints will be tested in a hierarchical order using the" "specified primary estimand analysis." "Only if the primary efficacy endpoint leads to a" "statistically significant result at the one-sided 2.5% level, will the key secondary endpoints be" "adjusted for multiplicity and tested in the sequential order specified in Panel 17." "If one of the" "endpoints in the testing procedure does not show superiority, then statistical significance in" "relation to multiplicity will not be declared for any of the subsequent key secondary" "endpoints, regardless of their p-values." "Panel 17: Multiple testing procedure for the primary and key secondary endpoints" "at Week 16." "The alternate hypothesis of a positive attributable treatment effect of" "placebo will be tested using 2-sided tests." "2-sided hypothesis tests can only show superiority" -- The primary endpoint is tested one-sided at 2.5% (exact decimal equivalent 0.025); only if it is significant is the 5% two-sided level passed to key secondary endpoints, tested in hierarchical sequential order with multiplicity adjustment. Panel 17’s detailed endpoint sequence is not available as selectable text, so no endpoint sequence is asserted.

study_schedule.source_excerpt: Sections 1.1, 1.2, 4.1, 4.4, 6.2.1; schedule synopsis and safety follow-up: "NCT number: NCT05958407" "Trial ID: LP0162-2328 Date: 13-Nov-2024 Version: 6.0" "Treatment For each subject, the trial will last at least 37 weeks and up to" "duration o a 1-to 4-week screening period" "o a 16-week double-blind treatment period" "o a 16-week open-label treatment period" "• The visit frequency will be every 2 weeks for the first 18 weeks," "then a visit after 6 weeks (Week 24), followed by visits every" "4 weeks; the Week 18, Week 28, and Week 36 visits are remote." "The primary endpoint is assessed at Week 16, and the final efficacy assessments will" "For each subject, the trial will last at least 37 weeks" "and up 40 weeks, including:" "• a 1-to 4-week screening period" "• a 16-week double-blind treatment period" "• a 16-week open-label treatment period" "• a 4-week safety follow-up period." "The screening period has a minimum duration of 1 week and a maximum duration of 4 weeks" "depending on the need for wash-out (i.e., the screening visit should take place between Week -" "4 and Week -1)." "Double-blind treatment period (Week 0 to Week 16)" "Open-label treatment period (Week 16 to Week 32)" "Safety follow-up period (Week 32 to Week 36)" "All subjects who complete the open-label treatment period (Week 32) will attend a safety" "follow-up visit (performed via phone, but can be performed as a site visit if needed) 6 weeks" "after the last IMP administration for assessment of safety." "The last administration of IMP under this protocol will occur at Week 30." -- The protocol identifies LP0162-2328 and NCT05958407, so the schedule is for this trial. Screening is stated as variable from 1 to 4 weeks (Week -4/-1 to Week 0); start_week -4 is the earliest boundary and duration_weeks remains null. The protocol's narrative gives a 16-week double-blind period (Weeks 0-16), a 16-week open-label period (Weeks 16-32), and a 4-week safety follow-up (Weeks 32-36). It explicitly says total participation is at least 37 and up to 40 weeks, so the schema's single integer total_duration_weeks is left null. Visits are every 2 weeks through the first 18 weeks, then Week 24, followed by every 4 weeks; the Week 18, 28, and 36 contacts are remote, matching CT.gov's three phone visits, and are in phone_contact_weeks. Week 36 is the safety follow-up contact: the final planned IMP administration is Week 30, making Week 36 six weeks later, while the 4-week follow-up period starts at Week 32 (2 weeks after last injection); these are compatible anchors, not a discrepancy. Clinic visits are Weeks 0-16, 24, and 32. The protocol text file references full schedules of activities, but does not contain their per-visit tables, so full_visit_table_available is false. The cited protocol explicitly places the primary endpoint at Week 16 and calls final efficacy assessments Week 32. No routine screening washout, follow-up visit interval, or long-term extension is asserted.

value.rationale: Rescue treatment is for intolerable AHE signs and symptoms, is prescribed at investigator discretion, and is recorded in the eCRF.

rescue_therapy.source_excerpt: 6.7.2 Rescue treatment: "Rescue treatment is defined as any treatment initiated to treat intolerable AHE signs and" "symptoms during the treatment and safety follow-up periods." "It will be recorded in the eCRF" "if a medication or procedure is given as rescue treatment." "If medically necessary (i.e., to treat intolerable AHE signs and symptoms), rescue treatment" "for AHE may be prescribed to trial subjects at the discretion of the investigator." -- The protocol permits investigator-discretion rescue treatment when medically necessary for intolerable AHE symptoms during treatment and safety follow-up. It is not a prohibition or fixed threshold rule.
